# op-runit-systemctl

D-Bus service exposing systemctl-style operations through the host's runit
supervisor. The service runs on Artix Linux; `sv` is the control tool, and
`s6`/`s6-rc` are not used as service managers here.

## D-Bus interface

| Property | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Bus name | `org.opdbus.v1.plugins.runit` |
| Object path | `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/runit` |
| Interface | `org.opdbus.v1.plugins.runit` |

Lifecycle methods (`start`, `stop`, `force_stop`, `restart`, `reload`,
`enable`, `disable`, and `daemon_reload`) require a root D-Bus caller. The
bridge remains responsible for its identity and capability checks; this
service also enforces the root caller boundary. Service names are validated
before being used as path components.

## Methods

| Method | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `start(service)` | Ensures the persistent runlevel symlink, then runs `sv up`. |
| `stop(service)` | Runs `sv down` for a service in the live runlevel. |
| `force_stop(service)` | Runs runit's `sv force-stop`. |
| `restart(service)` | Runs `sv restart`; if absent from the live runlevel, ensures its persistent symlink and runs `sv up`. |
| `reload(service)` | Sends `sv hup`. |
| `enable(service)` | Adds the persistent `default` runlevel symlink and removes the service's `down` marker. |
| `disable(service)` | Runs `sv down` when present in the live runlevel, then removes its persistent symlink. |
| `status(service)` | Returns JSON describing active state, sub-state, PID, readiness, and uptime. |
| `is_active(service)` | Returns `active` or `inactive`. |
| `is_enabled(service)` | Returns `enabled` or `disabled`. |
| `show(service)` | Returns systemctl-style service properties as JSON. |
| `list_units()` | Lists entries in the live runlevel as JSON. |
| `list_unit_files()` | Lists service definitions from `/etc/sv` as JSON. |
| `journalctl(service, lines)` | Returns the requested tail of an available runit log file as JSON. |
| `daemon_reload()` | Root-only no-op: runit notices runlevel directory changes without database recompilation. |
| `daemon_status()` | Reports whether runit supervision appears available. |
| `get_unit_type(service)` | Reads the optional `type` marker under the service definition; defaults to `longrun`. |

`status`, `show`, `list_units`, `list_unit_files`, and `journalctl` return JSON
strings. `is_active`, `is_enabled`, `daemon_status`, and `get_unit_type` return
plain strings. Lifecycle methods return a `(success, message)` pair. Errors are
returned in the method result; callers should not treat an error-shaped
response as a successful operation.

## Binaries

- `svd` is a D-Bus client for the runit interface; it connects to the system
  bus before dispatching a command. Its command list is shown by `svd help`.
  The client does not invoke `sv` directly.

## Build

Run Cargo from the repository root as the checkout owner:

```bash
cargo build -p op-runit-systemctl
CXXFLAGS="-include cstdint" cargo build -p op-runit-systemctl --release
```

Runtime service management is provided through D-Bus. Host service actions
must use the supported runit and identity/capability boundaries; do not use
`systemctl`, `s6`, or `service6`.

## Architecture

- The service exports the `org.opdbus.v1.plugins.runit` D-Bus interface.
- Lifecycle requests are restricted to root D-Bus callers, in addition to
  the bridge's identity and capability admission.
- `sv` manages live service state; `/etc/runit/runsvdir/default` holds
  persistent enablement.
- Runit has no compiled service database, so `daemon_reload` does not rebuild
  one.

## License

Apache-2.0

# op-runit-systemctl

D-Bus service exposing systemctl-style operations through the host's runit
supervisor. The service runs on Artix Linux; `sv` is the control tool, and
`s6`/`s6-rc` are not used as service managers here.

## D-Bus interface

| Property | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Bus name | `org.opdbus.v1.plugins.runit` |
| Object path | `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/runit` |
| Interface | `org.opdbus.v1.plugins.runit` |

Lifecycle methods (`start`, `stop`, `force_stop`, `restart`, `reload`,
`enable`, `disable`, and `daemon_reload`) require a root D-Bus caller. The
bridge remains responsible for its identity and capability checks; this
service also enforces the root caller boundary. Service names are validated
before being used as path components.

## Methods

| Method | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `start(service)` | Ensures the persistent runlevel symlink, then runs `sv up`. |
| `stop(service)` | Runs `sv down` for a service in the live runlevel. |
| `force_stop(service)` | Runs runit's `sv force-stop`. |
| `restart(service)` | Runs `sv restart`; if absent from the live runlevel, ensures its persistent symlink and runs `sv up`. |
| `reload(service)` | Sends `sv hup`. |
| `enable(service)` | Adds the persistent `default` runlevel symlink and removes the service's `down` marker. |
| `disable(service)` | Runs `sv down` when present in the live runlevel, then removes its persistent symlink. |
| `status(service)` | Returns JSON describing active state, sub-state, PID, readiness, and uptime. |
| `is_active(service)` | Returns `active` or `inactive`. |
| `is_enabled(service)` | Returns `enabled` or `disabled`. |
| `show(service)` | Returns systemctl-style service properties as JSON. |
| `list_units()` | Lists entries in the live runlevel as JSON. |
| `list_unit_files()` | Lists service definitions from `/etc/sv` as JSON. |
| `journalctl(service, lines)` | Returns the requested tail of an available runit log file as JSON. |
| `daemon_reload()` | Root-only no-op: runit notices runlevel directory changes without database recompilation. |
| `daemon_status()` | Reports whether runit supervision appears available. |
| `get_unit_type(service)` | Reads the optional `type` marker under the service definition; defaults to `longrun`. |

`status`, `show`, `list_units`, `list_unit_files`, and `journalctl` return JSON
strings. `is_active`, `is_enabled`, `daemon_status`, and `get_unit_type` return
plain strings. Lifecycle methods return a `(success, message)` pair. Errors are
returned in the method result; callers should not treat an error-shaped
response as a successful operation.

## Binaries

- `svd` is a D-Bus client for the runit interface; it connects to the system
  bus before dispatching a command. Its command list is shown by `svd help`.
  The client does not invoke `sv` directly.

## Build

Run Cargo from the repository root as the checkout owner:

```bash
cargo build -p op-runit-systemctl
CXXFLAGS="-include cstdint" cargo build -p op-runit-systemctl --release
```

Runtime service management is provided through D-Bus. Host service actions
must use the supported runit and identity/capability boundaries; do not use
`systemctl`, `s6`, or `service6`.

## Architecture

- The service exports the `org.opdbus.v1.plugins.runit` D-Bus interface.
- Lifecycle requests are restricted to root D-Bus callers, in addition to
  the bridge's identity and capability admission.
- `sv` manages live service state; `/etc/runit/runsvdir/default` holds
  persistent enablement.
- Runit has no compiled service database, so `daemon_reload` does not rebuild
  one.

## License

Apache-2.0
